baseline.name: Dense array with linear membership search
baseline.approach: Scan the array to find or reject a value; remove by swapping the last element; select a random index.
baseline.time: O(n) insert/remove membership checks, O(1) random lookup

archived.name: Dense array plus chained hash index
archived.time: Expected O(1) insert/remove, worst O(n) collision search; O(1) random lookup

why: The hash table finds a value's array slot without a full membership scan, and swap-and-pop keeps random lookup dense.
quantitative_comparison: The baseline may inspect n values per membership operation; the archive expects a short hash chain but can still inspect n nodes under collisions. No faster-percentage or worst-case constant-time claim is justified.
tradeoffs: Large fixed buffers/init costs may lose for small sets; capacity and allocations are unchecked. rand()%size requires a nonempty set and can introduce modulo bias rather than exact uniformity.
evidence_basis: Static expected-work comparison under distributed-hash assumptions; no runtime or random-distribution benchmark.
